scope.notes: Inventory in progress (57 rows). Covers Exalted: The Autochthonians' Chapter Two character-creation overview (Attributes/Abilities/Advantages/Virtues/Finishing Touches, plus the bonus-point and experience-cost tables), the universal Alchemical Anima Effect (the five-tier 1-3/4-7/8-10/11-15/16+ Anima Banner table and the Attribute-boost anima power available to every caste), the Alchemical Physiology section (Artificial Metabolism/feeding, Life and Death/dissolution, and Refitting/Essence Advancement/city-metamorphosis), all five Castes (Orichalcum, Moonsilver, Jade, Starmetal, Soulsteel) with their Caste Attributes/Anima Effects/Associations/Sobriquets/Concepts, the apocryphal sixth 'Adamant' Caste sidebar, the full Clarity Trait (the Limit analog: gaining, losing, the 0-10 effects table, and Storytelling guidance) plus its corrupted mirror Dissonance/Gremlin Syndrome, and the new/altered Backgrounds (Class, Vats, Artifact, Backing, Familiar, Manse) including the Building Vats in Creation sidebar and the Followers/Influence/Resources exclusion note. Chapter Three's Charm-system framing (Charm Slots/Panoplies/Submodules/Arrays, Designing New Charms, Eclipse/Moonshadow access, and the Charm format/limitations conventions), the two General Charms (Transitory and Sustained Augmentation of (Attribute)), the complete Close Combat Charms tree (15 Charms plus the Alchemical Martial Artists style-list sidebar, ending at Perfected Lotus Matrix), and the complete Ranged Combat Charms tree (11 Charms, ending at Dedicated Harmonic Targeting) are now inventoried. The Might and Mobility Charms tree onward (remaining Ability lines of Chapter Three), the Man-Machine/God-Machine Weaving Engine Charms and the full Alchemical weaving-protocol catalog (Chapter Four, pp. 145-159/PDF 146-160 per an in-book cross-reference), Chapter Four's remaining Miracles of the Machine God material, and the Locust War/Great Source/Engines of Extinction adventure chapters are not yet inventoried.

sources.role: Primary Alchemical rules, Charms, Backgrounds, and Autochthonia setting material

rulesNotes: This PDF has a real, clean, selectable text layer (it is not image-based). Text was extracted directly with PyMuPDF (fitz) and cross-checked against the on-page header, which prints the same page number as the 0-indexed PyMuPDF page across every chapter sampled (idx 2 through idx 300): printed page number = 0-indexed PDF page = (1-indexed physical PDF page) - 1. Equivalently, pdfPage (1-indexed, as recorded on every citation below) = printedPage + 1, with no additional front-matter shift anywhere in the book.

Because the text layer is clean, extracted text counts as having been read for every row below. In addition, the tables and several Caste pages that are most vulnerable to multi-column extraction order problems (the Class dot table, the Familiar dot table, the Vats dot table, the Building Vats sidebar, the Clarity effects table, the Alchemical Anima Banners table, and the Orichalcum/Starmetal/Soulsteel Caste pages) were also rendered to page images and visually compared against the extracted text; the extraction matched the rendered pages exactly everywhere it was spot-checked.

The family in this repository's data model is named `alchemical`, but the source book's real title is 'Exalted: The Autochthonians' (not 'The Alchemicals'). bookId/bookLabel use the real title, matching the correction already applied once before in this project.

Alchemicals do not have a Limit Trait. The book's own name for the signature trait mechanic is Clarity (a corrupted, actively malicious mirror version exists too, called Dissonance, gained only via the Gremlin Syndrome Flaw). See the clarity-* and gremlin-syndrome-dissonance rows.

The book still calls Alchemical Exalted's innate magic 'Charms' (it does not rename them), but every Charm is a surgically implanted artifact occupying a General or Dedicated Charm Slot rather than being learned outright the way other Exalted's Charms are. Chapter Three (pp. 87-141/PDF 88-142) organizes Charms into named per-Attribute-cluster trees (General Charms, then Close Combat, Ranged Combat, Might and Mobility, and further trees not yet inventoried) rather than by Ability the way Solar/Abyssal Charms are; each tree's own tree diagram was visually cross-checked against the extracted text everywhere it was sampled and matched exactly.

The Man-Machine Weaving Engine and God-Machine Weaving Engine are ordinary Chapter Three Charms (Essence and Weaving Charms sub-tree, the chapter's final section, p. 141/PDF 142) that merely let an installed Alchemical initiate a 'protocol' of Alchemical weaving she has separately learned; the full weaving-protocol catalog itself (the actual list of Man-Machine and God-Machine protocols and their effects) is explicitly cross-referenced in-book to pp. 145-159 (PDF 146-160), which falls in Chapter Four (Miracles of the Machine God), not Chapter Three. Both Engine Charms and the full protocol catalog remain out of scope for this pass; see the README's 'What's still needed' list for the precise resume point.

Checked for additional Alchemical-only Merits/Flaws beyond Gremlin Syndrome by full-text-searching 'merit'/'flaw' across Chapter Two's edges (PDF 56-90) and all of Chapter Three (PDF 87-142); no further Alchemical-specific Merit or Flaw exists in either range. Gremlin Syndrome/Dissonance remains the only one in this book.
